Run a Model Context Protocol server over stdio for AI agents

Run a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server on stdin and stdout, so that an AI
agent (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code and other MCP clients) can
use Repsy through rp. The client starts the process itself; you do not run it
by hand. Configure the client to run:

```
rp mcp
```

and select the profile as for any other command (--hostname or REPSY_HOST).
The server signs every request with the credential of that profile:
REPSY_TOKEN when it is set, else the credential stored by rp auth login.

stdout carries the protocol only: rp prints nothing else there, never prompts
and never reads anything but protocol messages from stdin. Messages for a
person go to stderr. The server ends when the client closes stdin.

The tools that change the registry are offered only while the credential may
use them: a login session (rp auth login) may use all of them; an access token
needs repo:write for trigger_scan and repo:manage for every other one. A
repo:read token sees only the read tools. The server checks the credential
again while it runs and tells the client when the list changes. --read-only
hides every tool that changes the registry, whatever the credential may do.

The ones that can be changed back (create_repo, trigger_scan, update_repo,
update_repo_settings, update_proxy_settings, set_docker_cleanup_policy) are
plain write tools. Every other one deletes, revokes, rotates, grants access,
opens a repository, redirects data or creates a secret: it is annotated
destructive, so clients always ask before calling it, and it repeats its
target in a confirm argument. The tools for collaborators, webhooks and proxy
upstreams work on Repsy Cloud only.

A secret a tool creates (create_deploy_token, rotate_deploy_token,
create_webhook, rotate_webhook_secret, create_access_token,
rotate_access_token) is in the tool's result, so it enters the conversation
and the transcript of the client. A personal access token created here keeps
working after the conversation ends, until it expires or is revoked.

rp mcp tools lists the tools, and the reference page "MCP tools" describes
each of them with its arguments.

Requests carry "mcp" in the User-Agent.

```
rp mcp [flags]
```

## Options

```
      --read-only   Offer only the read tools, whatever the credential may do
```
